title: Canonical identity and composition comparisons for algebraic-space derived pullback
statement: For algebraic spaces over a scheme S [def-trf-algebraic-space], use the existing canonical tensor pullback on module sheaves and its local pure tensor sections [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use the existing small ringed model equivalences [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], unbounded derived categories [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the canonical total left derived tensor pullback Lf* with its counit Q Lf*→F_f, where F_f is the existing termwise small-model tensor pullback followed by localization [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback]. Write spaceDerivedPullback for this same existing Lf* with a common localization morphism universe w. For f:X→Y and g:Z→X, use the already specified ordinary tensor composition comparison sending c⊗(b⊗m) to c g♯(b)⊗m [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition]. There is a unique ordinary identity comparison (id_X)*≅id sending b⊗m to b times the restriction of m on every chart; retain it. Transport the existing composition comparison and this identity comparison through the small-model equivalences using their unit and counit. The composite Lf* followed by Lg* is universal for F_(g f), with the comparison made from both existing derived counits and the transported ordinary composition comparison. Define L(g f)*≅Lf* Lg* by uniqueness with these precise counits. The identity functor is universal for F_(id_X) with the inverse ordinary multiplication comparison on complexes; define L(id_X)*≅id by uniqueness. These comparison constructions are unbounded, allow arbitrary common localization morphism universe w, and impose no flatness assumption on f or g.
